headline: ENERGY FUELS TARGETS 1M LBS AT WHITE MESA IN DEC CAMPAIGN — Pinyon Plain + La Sal Feed Supplies Utility Contracts Through 2028
snippet: Energy Fuels (TSX: EFR / NYSE: UUUU) announced a new uranium processing campaign at its White Mesa Mill in Utah — the largest conventional uranium facility in the US — targeting approximately one million pounds of U₃O₈ from December 2026 through Q1 2027. Feedstock will draw from the Pinyon Plain mine in Arizona and the La Sal Complex in Utah. Production supports existing utility supply contracts through 2028; output has been left largely unhedged in anticipation of higher uranium prices. White Mesa processing costs remain between $9–$12/lb, among the lowest in the industry.

headline: GOLD WEEKLY: AFTER 9% PLUNGE, PCE INFLATION IS THE KEY TEST — Analysts Set $3,400–$3,500 Near-Term Target; Dec 8-9 Fed Meeting Decides Direction
snippet: FX Empire's weekly gold forecast sets a short-term downside target of $3,400–$3,500, noting that Friday's PCE inflation data is the next major catalyst after gold's worst week of 2026. The 10-year Treasury yield dropped from a 5.17% weekly high to 4.91%, providing marginal relief — but the analyst remains neutral on gold over the medium term. The December 8-9 Federal Reserve meeting is identified as the defining event for gold's direction over the next three to six months. A sustained recovery above $3,650 would be required to shift the technical picture back to bullish.

headline: USFM SIGNS TERM SHEET FOR 85% OF PERMITTED HOOK LAKE — Nunavut Gold-Copper VMS Project Advances in Junior Arctic M&A
snippet: USFM signed a non-binding term sheet today to acquire up to 85% of the Hook Lake Project in Nunavut, Canada — a fully permitted gold and copper volcanogenic massive sulphide project with a historical estimate of approximately 285,000 ounces of gold at the Turquetil Lake deposit. Hook Lake is located in eastern Nunavut and hosts several additional polymetallic VMS prospects. The term sheet marks an early-stage M&A step; binding definitive agreements would follow subject to due diligence, board approval, and exchange consent.

headline: URANIUM ONE TAPS ATHABASCA VETERAN FOR PASFIELD LAKE — Geophysicist Jeremy Brett Joins Technical Advisory to Advance Saskatchewan Exploration
snippet: Uranium One (OTC: UUUFF) appointed senior geophysicist Jeremy S. Brett to its technical advisory board to assist with historical record reviews and exploration planning at the Pasfield Lake project in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin — one of the world's premier uranium-hosting geological settings. The appointment signals active exploration intent at Pasfield Lake as the company builds technical capacity for the next phase of drill targeting in the Basin.

headline: RADIUS GOLD MAPS MULTI-KILOMETER HYDROTHERMAL FOOTPRINT AT TIERRA ROJA, PERU — Multi-Center Intrusive Complex Identified, Drilling Targets Taking Shape
snippet: Radius Gold (TSX-V: RDU) reported expanded multi-element geochemical sampling and alteration mapping at its Tierra Roja copper project in Peru, outlining a hydrothermal alteration footprint spanning several kilometres. The data points to a partially unroofed multi-center intrusive complex — a geological configuration associated with porphyry copper systems. The expanded footprint increases the scale of the mineralizing system relative to earlier models and is being used to define priority drill targets for the next field campaign.

headline: TRIFECTA GOLD SECURES NON-DILUTIVE FINANCING TO RE-FOCUS ON MT. HINTON — TSX-V Junior Avoids Equity Raise in Tough Financing Market
snippet: Trifecta Gold (TSX-V: TG) announced it will re-focus its exploration program at the Mt. Hinton gold project using non-dilutive financing, sidestepping the equity raises that have squeezed junior exploration companies in the current market environment. The move is notable given the broader junior financing freeze highlighted at this month's Deutsche Goldmesse, where analysts noted explorers are struggling to close even sub-$3 million equity rounds. Non-dilutive structures — royalty deals, streams, or debt — preserve shareholder value and reflect a shift in how cashed-out juniors are funding programs through the correction.

headline: SILVER DOWN 60% FROM HIGH AS GOLD-SILVER RATIO HITS 85.8 — Two Industrial Demand Pressures That Could Keep Silver Lagging Into 2027
snippet: With silver at approximately $41.25 — down more than 60% from its 2026 high — and the gold-silver ratio at 85.8 (well above its long-term average near 55), analysts are examining whether silver will recover its typical outperformance. ActionForex identifies two industrial headwinds that may keep silver lagging: weakening solar panel installation growth in China and softening EV output forecasts both trim demand for silver's industrial applications. A gold-silver ratio this high has historically preceded sharp silver recoveries — but only once monetary tightening expectations peak.

headline: THANKSGIVING WEEK: CPI WEDNESDAY AND THIN LIQUIDITY FRAME GOLD'S CRITICAL NEXT MOVE — Holiday Market Could Amplify Any Surprise
snippet: With US markets closed Thursday for Thanksgiving and expected to thin through Friday, Wednesday's CPI release is the pivotal event of the holiday week for gold and mining stocks. FXStreet flags that reduced liquidity amplifies price moves in either direction — a hot CPI print in thin trading would accelerate the selloff, while a soft reading could produce an outsized short-covering bounce. Philadelphia Fed commentary calling for another rate hike has reinforced the bearish near-term setup, but oversold technical conditions create a hair-trigger for a reversal.

headline: WHY GOLD AND SILVER MINERS FALL 2–3X HARDER THAN THE METALS IN SELLOFFS — The Structural Leverage That Retail Investors Underestimate
snippet: An Investing.com analysis explains why gold and silver mining equities are falling two to three times harder than the underlying metals: miners carry fixed operating costs — labour, energy, reagents, royalties — that don't decline with metal prices. Each dollar drop in gold hits revenue directly but leaves cost structures unchanged, compressing margins on a leveraged basis. The same mechanism works in reverse on the upside, but in the current AI-led forced liquidation and rising rate environment, operational leverage is working against shareholders of both majors and juniors alike.

headline: GOLD, SILVER, OIL OUTLOOK AS 97% DEC RATE HIKE BETS RESHAPE RESOURCE POSITIONING — What Fed Hawkishness Means for Junior Miners
snippet: Discovery Alert's analysis walks through the implications of near-certainty pricing (97% CME odds) for a December Federal Reserve rate hike across gold, silver, oil, and mining equities. The piece argues that rate hike certainty is already priced in and that the remaining downside risk comes from deteriorating macro data, not additional Fed hawkishness — meaning junior miners levered to gold and copper could stabilize or rebound sharply if December CPI and PCE prints undershoot consensus. Oil's response to the same rate signals differs from gold, providing context for energy-exposed mining jurisdictions.
